claude.performance_metric: Full divestiture of combined Eagle Ford position (incl. WildHorse/Brazos Valley acreage) across three 2023 transactions, ~$3.5bn aggregate consideration, ~$947m aggregate gains
claude.rationale: The slice documents only reporting-status and asset-tracking outcomes: the Brazos Valley area was disclosed distinctly through FY2020, folded into the combined "Eagle Ford" line by the FY2021 10-K "does not state explicitly why," and the whole position was divested in 2023. Nothing in the slice documents a realized disruption at the product/process interface (product-operations incoherence), so p4 is left uncertain given the filings explicitly do not isolate cause or WildHorse-specific attribution. Likewise no documented operations-vs-organization/culture fracture is described; the Chapter 11 filing and reorganization are noted as outside the fixed window and are not tied to any process/organization integration breakdown, so p5 is uncertain rather than 0. The slice provides no evidence bearing on controlling-intent archetype coherence or business-model reconcilability.

grok.performance_metric: combined Eagle Ford (incl. acquired) fully divested 2023 ~$3.5bn
grok.rationale: The slice documents that Brazos Valley was carried as a distinct operating area through FY2019–FY2020, folded into combined Eagle Ford reporting by FY2021, and that the combined Eagle Ford position was fully divested in three 2023 transactions; it does not document any product/process misalignment or inability to align the acquired acreage with operating processes over time, so p4_pathway=0. No evidence is given of operations-versus-organization/culture fracture specific to integrating the acquired business (Chapter 11 naming of Brazos Valley entities is acquirer-wide insolvency context, not a realized process/organization interface disruption), so p5_pathway=0.

openai.performance_metric: Combined Eagle Ford position fully divested in 2023 for approximately $3.5 billion
openai.rationale: The FY2021 annual report shows that Brazos Valley had been folded into the combined Eagle Ford reporting line, but it gives no indication of product-line or operating-process incoherence. The FY2023 10-K documents the complete divestiture of the combined Eagle Ford position but does not attribute it to product/process failure or to conflict involving personnel, management, or culture. Accordingly, neither a p4 nor a p5 disruption is documented.
